stem:
Pallavi notes the Moon's place in the sky from her balcony in Nagpur at 8:30 p.m. on Friday. She checks again at 8:30 p.m. on Saturday.

What should she expect?

options.text: The Moon will be in exactly the same place in the sky both nights.
The Moon will most likely appear in a different part of the sky.
The Moon must rise exactly when the Sun sets on both nights.
The Moon's sky place never changes from one day to the next at the same clock time.

teacher.key_rationale: The Moon advances in its orbit while Earth rotates, so at the same clock time on successive days it appears in a different sky position and does not always rise at sunset. A and D deny that day-to-day shift; C ties moonrise to sunset every day.
